logline: Two childhood friends reunite as adults after a complete reversal of fortune - she once beautiful now plain, he once awkward now polished - complicated by mistaken identity and workplace hierarchy.

renewal.note: Single-season run of 16 episodes concluded on November 11, 2015. No sequel has been produced.

bollymeter.basis: Peaked at 18.4 percent domestic viewership and an IMDb score of 7.5; reviewers praised its consistent comic energy and lead chemistry while noting the 16-episode run stretches its central premise thin.

seasons.review_body: She Was Pretty aired on MBC from September to November 2015 and peaked at 18.4 percent nationally, ranking among the network's stronger prime-time performers that year. The series built its audience on Park Seo-joon and Hwang Jung-eum's comedic chemistry - the show generates sustained laugh-out-loud moments unusual in the genre. The mistaken-identity premise slots into a classic romcom template, and the fashion-magazine workplace backdrop gave it a visual sparkle that translated well internationally, particularly in China. The script runs short of fresh complications around episode 12, leaning on misunderstanding loops in its back half; at 16 episodes the premise stretches. The 7.5 IMDb score sits in a range consistent with charming-but-unambitious romcoms.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 1
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The premiere sets up its role-reversal premise briskly and introduces the mistaken-identity complication with enough wit to hook casual romcom viewers immediately.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The first office encounter where the heroine realises her childhood sweetheart is now her tyrannical boss - the source of the series' central comic and romantic tension.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 16
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The finale wraps its love triangle with clean resolution and delivers the emotional payoff for viewers who backed the lead couple across the show's full run.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The confession scene that finally strips away all pretence between the leads.
